source.version: Journal version of record: Scientific Reports (2024) 14:18525, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-024-69423-2; received 15 March 2024, accepted 5 August 2024, published online 9 August 2024 (p. 9). Publisher PDF retrieved via the KU Leuven Lirias repository.
source.title_on_document: Establishing the importance of co-creation and self-efficacy in creative collaboration with artificial intelligence

supplement.where: The paper refers to no supplementary information. Data and syntax files are on OSF: https://osf.io/3jqga/ (p. 2; p. 8 Methods; p. 9 Data availability).
supplement.holds: No supplement. The OSF repository holds data and SPSS syntax, from which participant-level standard errors could be computed. The main text gives arm means, SDs, ns, ANOVA F tests, and pairwise p-values (Tables 1 and 2).

paper_design_summary: Two online experiments on Prolific in which English-speaking adults wrote an 8-line poem. Study 1 randomly assigned participants to write alone or to edit a poem produced by a neural poetry generation system (with line alternatives), and added 50 poems generated by the system alone as a benchmark. Study 2 randomly assigned participants to write alone, to edit the AI poem (as in Study 1), or to co-create line by line with a redesigned interface; in both studies 10 professional poets rated each poem's creativity on a 1-40 scale (Consensual Assessment Technique).

studies.label: Study 1 (poetry writing: alone vs editing an AI-generated poem; AI-only benchmark poems)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Condition: human (write the poem unassisted) vs human-AI (receive a poem generated by the AI poetry system and edit it freely with line-alternative tools). The AI condition is 50 poems generated by the system alone, with no participants.
assignment.quote: Participants were randomly allocated to one of two experimental condition groups.
assignment.locator: p. 2, Results, Study 1; also p. 9, Methods: "Condition assignments were random in both studies, with randomization administered via front-end programming."

arms.name: Human condition
arms.description: Wrote an 8-line poem (two 4-line stanzas) unassisted, no time limit.

arms.name: Human-AI condition (editor)
arms.description: Received a poem generated by the neural poetry system and could edit any line, pick alternative lines from a dropdown that updated in real time and kept the ABAB rhyme, or delete and start from scratch. No time limit.

arms.name: AI condition (benchmark)
arms.description: Poems generated entirely by the poetry generation system (n = 50 poems). No human participants; included as a benchmark for the expert ratings.

participants.exclusions: 101 recruited; six failed an instrumental attention check and were removed, leaving 96 analyzed (48 per human arm). Note 101 - 6 = 95, not 96, as printed. The paper does not say whether the attention check came before or after assignment, so no randomized count is recorded. The 50 AI-condition poems are not people.
participants.who: Prolific participants whose first language is English, approval rating at least 97 percent; mean age 27.23 (SD 8.97), 76 percent female; paid GBP 2.50.
participants.quote: Participants were 101 individuals recruited via Prolific Academic in exchange for GBP2.50 (approximately USD3.00). Six participants failed to correctly answer an instrumental attention check and were removed from subsequent analyses
participants.locator: p. 2, Results, Study 1; p. 8-9, Methods (eligibility, attention check, approval rating)

ai_tool.name_model: Neural poetry generation system of Van de Cruys (2020): recurrent neural encoder-decoder trained on 500 million words of CommonCrawl prose, with rhyme (ABAB) and NMF topic constraints; topic set randomly chosen from 100 sets of three words in Study 1.
ai_tool.how_used: The system supplied a complete 8-line poem as the default; participants edited it directly or swapped lines from a dropdown of AI-generated alternatives. Codebook roles fit poorly: the AI produced the draft and the person edited it (closest is ideas_supplied or other); recorded as refinement with this caveat, see open_questions.

task.description: Write an 8-line poem in two stanzas of four lines; rhyme optional.

outcomes.name: Expert evaluations of creativity (CAT), human-AI vs human
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Consensual Assessment Technique: 10 professional published poets (6 with graduate degrees in creative writing, English literature, or related) rated each of 146 poems for creativity on a 1-40 scale, blind to authorship, in random orders, told to use the full range. How the 10 ratings are aggregated per poem is not stated; inter-rater reliability not reported.

contrasts.reported: Human 18.23 (SD 4.94, n = 48) vs human-AI 12.55 (SD 4.32, n = 48), p < 0.001 (post hoc pairwise); omnibus one-way ANOVA across three groups F(2, 145) = 63.48, p < 0.001, partial eta2 = 0.47

outcomes.name: Expert evaluations of creativity, AI-only poems vs human and human-AI poems
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Same CAT ratings as S1-O1. The AI-only poems are a benchmark with no participants.

outcomes.name: Self-reported creativity of own poem
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: "rate the extent to which you think the poem you submitted is creative" (1-40). Self-report; does not meet criterion 3. Listed for completeness.

contrasts.reported: Human 23.88 (SD 8.40) vs human-AI 19.13 (SD 10.40), independent samples t-test p = 0.016, Cohen's D = 0.47

studies.label: Study 2 (poetry writing: alone vs editor vs co-creator with AI)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Condition: human (unassisted), human-AI (editor, same system and interface as Study 1), or co-creator human-AI (redesigned interface: participant picks the topic words and writes line 1, the system returns the next line, turns alternate, all lines editable).
assignment.quote: Participants were randomly allocated to one of three experimental condition groups.
assignment.locator: p. 4, Results, Study 2; also p. 9, Methods: "Condition assignments were random in both studies, with randomization administered via front-end programming."

arms.name: Human-AI condition (editor)
arms.description: Same poetry system and editing interface as Study 1: received a finished AI poem and edited it.

arms.name: Co-creator human-AI condition
arms.description: Redesigned interface: participant chose a set of three topic words from 100 sets, wrote the first line, and the system returned the next line, alternating until 8 lines; alternative candidate lines available and every line editable.

participants.exclusions: None: no participant failed the attention check (p. 4; p. 9). Arm ns 51 + 50 + 51 = 152; ANOVA df F(2, 149) consistent with 152.
participants.who: Prolific participants whose first language is English, approval rating at least 97 percent; mean age 35.11 (SD 12.06), 34.9 percent female; paid GBP 2.50.
participants.quote: Participants were 152 individuals recruited via Prolific Academic in exchange for GBP2.50 (approximately USD3.00). No participants failed to correctly answer an instrumental attention check.
participants.locator: p. 4, Results, Study 2; arm ns p. 4-5

ai_tool.name_model: Same neural poetry generation system as Study 1 (Van de Cruys 2020, recurrent encoder-decoder with rhyme and topic constraints), in two interfaces.
ai_tool.how_used: Editor arm: AI supplies the full poem and the person edits it (as in Study 1). Co-creator arm: turn-taking, the person writes a line and the AI generates the next line, with alternative candidate lines; closest codebook role is suggestions. Roles differ by arm, see open_questions.

task.description: Write an 8-line poem in two stanzas of four lines (same procedure as Study 1).
task.duration: No time limit (same procedure as Study 1).

company_involvement.description: Funded by the Ministry of Education, Singapore (11/2019/115); authors declare no competing interests. The AI system is an academic model built by co-author Van de Cruys.

eligibility.reason: Both studies randomly assigned individuals to write a poem with or without an AI poetry generator (p. 2, p. 4, p. 9). Study 2 analyzed 152 people (51/50/51) and Study 1 analyzed 96 people in the two human arms; both exceed 50. Creativity of each poem was rated by 10 professional poets (CAT). One caveat for Review 1: the AI is a 2020 recurrent encoder-decoder poetry generator, not an LLM chatbot; the paper calls it generative AI, and it generates text, so it is treated as in scope.

one_line_finding: Editing an AI-generated poem lowered expert-rated creativity relative to writing alone (Study 1: 12.55 vs 18.23 on 1-40, p < 0.001; Study 2: 12.53 vs 15.74, p = 0.001), while co-creating line by line with the AI scored 14.70, above editing (p = 0.026) and not different from writing alone (p = 0.278) (Tables 1 and 2, pp. 4 and 7).
open_questions: Scope: the AI tool is a recurrent neural encoder-decoder poetry generator (Van de Cruys 2020) trained on CommonCrawl prose, not a modern LLM. Does it count as generative AI under the codebook's scope (systems that produce text from a prompt)?

AI role coding: the editor arm (AI supplies a full poem, person edits) fits none of the codebook roles cleanly; recorded as refinement for Study 1, though refinement is defined as AI editing the person's draft. The co-creator arm is closest to suggestions. Reviewer should pick roles per arm.
Study 1 count inconsistency: 101 recruited minus 6 excluded = 95, but the paper reports 96 remaining (48 + 48). ANOVA F(2, 145) implies 148 observations, while 48 + 48 + 50 = 146 poems.

Study 2 human-condition SD for expert evaluations: text prints SD = 9.24 (p. 6), Table 2 prints 4.98 (p. 7). 9.24 is the human-condition SD for self-reported creativity, so the text value looks like a typo; Table 2 used here.

Primary record choice for Study 2: the paper's hypothesis is co-creator vs editor (ai_design). Under codebook rule 3, the arm closest to free use of a chatbot vs no AI would supply the ai_vs_bau primary record; neither AI arm is free chat.

Standard errors: all pairwise contrasts give only p-values (post hoc LSD tests). Per-participant analysis (one poem per person) means arm means/SDs/ns support d at the participant level; OSF data would allow SEs.
notes: Each participant wrote one poem, so poem-level and participant-level analyses coincide for the human arms; unit coded output because Study 1's ANOVA pools the 50 AI-only poems with participant poems. Creative self-efficacy (Study 2, three-item Tierney and Farmer scale, alpha = 0.92) is a self-reported mediator, not an output score; not listed as an outcome: human 4.71 (1.45), co-creator 4.62 (1.43), editor 3.74 (1.43), F(2, 149) = 7.01, p = 0.001 (p. 5, Figure 3, Table 2). Preregistration is not mentioned; the paper states "All conditions, measures and exclusions are reported" (p. 2). No diversity outcome and no after-AI outcome. Holzner et al. 2025 lists this paper as HAI10 and CP03 (from candidates.json leads, not verified here).
